meta.disclaimer: Recommendations are general agronomic guidance based on Texas thresholds, not a substitute for a certified agronomist or lab. Verify before large purchases.

field_recommendations.title: Reduce salinity (leach + drain)
field_recommendations.action: Leach salts with good-quality water once drainage is adequate (apply ~6 in extra water to push salts below the root zone).
field_recommendations.rate: Leaching fraction sized to soil; add drainage if water ponds.
field_recommendations.timing: Pre-season, when you can move water through the profile.
field_recommendations.notes: Test your IRRIGATION water too -- Brazos water in the Fort Bend/Richmond reach runs saltier downstream, so over-irrigating with it adds salt. Meanwhile grow salt-tolerant cotton or sorghum.
field_recommendations.addresses: Salinity is high (EC 6.0 dS/m); salt stress reduces water uptake and yield.

field_recommendations.title: Lower pH / manage alkalinity
field_recommendations.action: Apply elemental sulfur and use acidifying fertilizers (ammonium sulfate). On calcareous Blackland clay, fully lowering pH is slow and costly -- lean on tolerant crops + chelated micronutrients instead.
field_recommendations.timing: Apply and incorporate several months ahead; oxidation to acid takes weeks-months and warm soil.
field_recommendations.notes: Test for free lime first. If the soil fizzes with acid it is calcareous and sulfur demand is very high -- prefer cotton, sorghum and other alkaline-tolerant crops.
field_recommendations.addresses: Soil is too alkaline (pH 8.1); iron, phosphorus and zinc become less available.

field_recommendations.title: Correct nitrogen deficiency
field_recommendations.action: Apply nitrogen fertilizer (urea 46-0-0 or UAN). Split the application on corn/leafy crops to limit leaching.
field_recommendations.timing: At/near planting; split-apply for corn (pre-plant + side-dress).
field_recommendations.notes: Rate sized to a generic ~40 ppm soil-N target; specify a crop for a tailored rate. A legume cover crop can fix 40-100 lb N/acre biologically and cut this bill over time.
field_recommendations.addresses: Nitrogen is deficient (12 ppm); expect pale, stunted growth.

field_recommendations.title: Correct phosphorus deficiency
field_recommendations.action: Band phosphate (DAP 18-46-0 or triple superphosphate) near the seed row for best early uptake.
field_recommendations.notes: Banding beats broadcasting on high-pH soils where P gets tied up.
field_recommendations.addresses: Phosphorus is deficient (9 ppm); poor root and early growth.

field_recommendations.title: Stop over-applying phosphorus
field_recommendations.action: Halt all P fertilizer and manure. Protect water: buffer strips, cover crops, and erosion control to stop P-laden runoff.
field_recommendations.rate: 0 lb P2O5/acre until soil test P drops below 150 ppm.
field_recommendations.notes: High P is a runoff / water-quality liability, not a yield gain. Draw it down through crop removal over several seasons.
field_recommendations.addresses: Phosphorus is very high (165 ppm); runoff and water-quality risk, wasted inputs.

recommendations.title: Lower pH / manage alkalinity
recommendations.action: Apply elemental sulfur and use acidifying fertilizers (ammonium sulfate). On calcareous Blackland clay, fully lowering pH is slow and costly -- lean on tolerant crops + chelated micronutrients instead.
